title: Phnom Penh International Half Marathon 2027: Cambodia's Capital Gets a Flagship 21K
seo_title: Phnom Penh Half Marathon 2027 Review | Date & Course Guide
meta_description: An early look at the Phnom Penh International Half Marathon, set for 13 June 2027 at Botumvatey Pagoda Park. Cambodia Events brings its formula to the capital — here's what we know so far.
dek: Set for June 2027 at Phnom Penh's Botumvatey Pagoda Park, this half marathon comes from Cambodia Events — the same team behind the Sihanoukville International Half Marathon and the Angkor Empire Marathon. Registration hasn't opened yet. Here's what the early intelligence says and why the organiser's track record matters more than the missing sign-up page.
verdict: The Phnom Penh International Half Marathon is less a race to register for today and more a race to bookmark. The organiser is Cambodia Events, the team behind two of the country's most established road races — the Sihanoukville International Half Marathon, now entering its 12th edition, and the Angkor Empire Marathon — and this is their first move into the capital. With registration not yet open and no route map published for a June 2027 date, the intelligence is genuinely thin. But the organiser's decade-plus track record with Cambodian heritage races, combined with a flat capital-city course and a pagoda-park start line, makes this worth watching. Treat it as a calendar placeholder, not a locked-in race-cation, and check the official Cambodia Events site as details land.

sections.heading: The Setting: Botumvatey Pagoda Park and a Flat Capital Canvas
paragraphs: The race is anchored at Botumvatey Pagoda Park, a landscaped green space in the heart of Phnom Penh named after the adjacent Wat Botum — one of the city's oldest and most significant Buddhist temples. [1] It's the kind of venue that signals a race aiming for atmosphere over pure speed: tree-lined grounds, temple spires on the skyline, and enough open space for a proper start-and-finish precinct rather than a squeezed-pavement setup.

Phnom Penh itself sits on the Mekong's west bank at an elevation that barely registers — the city core is pancake-flat, which means the half marathon route, when published, is unlikely to trouble anyone with elevation unless organisers deliberately route it toward the few bridge crossings or landfill rises on the outskirts. The trade-off, as with any Cambodian city race, will be heat rather than hills.

sections.heading: The Organiser: Cambodia Events Brings Its Formula to the Capital
paragraphs: The single most consequential fact about this race isn't on any registration page — it's who's running it. The organiser is Cambodia Events, the same team behind the Sihanoukville International Half Marathon (now in its 12th edition) and the Angkor Empire Marathon. [1] Those two races account for a substantial slice of Cambodia's road-running calendar outside of the National Olympic Committee's Angkor Wat event.

That track record matters because it means the Phnom Penh edition isn't a cold start. Sihanoukville has iterated across more than a decade — the 2026 edition significantly rerouted toward the coastline after years of runner feedback about hills — and the Angkor Empire Marathon has used the same cambodia-events.org infrastructure to handle registration, timing, and logistics across multiple editions. [1] If even a fraction of that institutional knowledge transfers to the capital, runners can expect functional organisation rather than first-edition chaos. One Sihanoukville finisher described it as a race where 'the ambiance carries the day,' which is a realistic benchmark for what Cambodia Events delivers: competent, community-minded, not slick. [1]

sections.heading: What's Missing: Registration, Route Maps, and the June Weather Question
paragraphs: As of August 2026, registration for the June 2027 race has not been announced, and no route map or elevation profile has been published. [1] For a race roughly ten months out, that's not unusual — Cambodian races in this organiser's stable have historically opened registration closer to race day — but it does mean anyone hoping to lock in travel plans early is working with a placeholder rather than a confirmed entry.

The June date also warrants attention. June sits inside Cambodia's wet season, which runs from May through October, and while mornings are typically drier than afternoons, the humidity in Phnom Penh in June is genuinely high. A pre-dawn flag-off — standard practice for Cambodian road races — will be essential, but runners should budget for a sweat-heavy morning regardless of when the gun goes off. [1] For context, Sihanoukville's half marathon has historically flagged off around 5:10–5:30am to beat the coastal heat, and a similar early-window strategy is likely here.

sections.heading: The Distances: A Familiar Three-Tier Spread
paragraphs: The event offers three distances: a 21.1km half marathon, a 10km race, and a 5km race — the same three-tier format Cambodia Events runs at its other races. [1] That spread makes it accessible across abilities: first-timers can step into the 5km or 10km, while experienced half-marathoners get a capital-city 21K without committing to a full marathon distance.

Cut-off times haven't been published yet, but for reference, Cambodia Events' Sihanoukville half marathon has historically used generous windows that accommodate walk-run participants across all three distances. Expect a relaxed, inclusive time policy rather than a hard, competitive cut — this organiser builds races for broad participation, not elite-only fields. [1]

sections.heading: Should You Bookmark It?
paragraphs: If you're looking for a race to register for right now, this isn't it — the sign-up window hasn't opened, the route isn't published, and there are no independent runner reports to draw on. But if you're building a 2027 race calendar and want a capital-city half marathon in a country whose running scene is quietly gaining momentum beyond Angkor Wat, the Phnom Penh International Half Marathon is worth a placeholder.

The organiser's track record is the real story here. Cambodia Events has kept Sihanoukville iterating for over a decade and the Angkor Empire Marathon running across multiple editions, and if they bring even a portion of that experience to Phnom Penh, the result should be a competent, community-flavoured city race with a pagoda-park start line and a flat, accessible course. Check the official Cambodia Events site as the race date approaches, and treat the thin early intelligence as a reminder to watch for updates rather than a reason to write the race off.
The 2027 edition is set for 13 June 2027 at Botumvatey Pagoda Park, Phnom Penh. [1]
